title: Zellij crashes at start, load in the sky
body:
Zellij 0.36.0 crashes at startup with

```
Received empty message from server
```

and load on my device goes up to over 20. This happened after a fresh boot.

**In Case of Graphical or Performance Issues**

`/tmp/zellij-1000/zellij-log/`:

```
INFO   |zellij_client            | 2023-05-30 18:13:53.281 [main      ] [zellij-client/src/lib.rs:143]: Starting Zellij client! 
INFO   |zellij_server            | 2023-05-30 18:13:53.290 [main      ] [zellij-server/src/lib.rs:237]: Starting Zellij server! 
INFO   |zellij_server            | 2023-05-30 18:13:53.345 [main      ] [zellij-server/src/lib.rs:843]: Compiling plugins using Cranelift 
INFO   |zellij_server::plugins   | 2023-05-30 18:13:53.346 [wasm      ] [zellij-server/src/plugins/mod.rs:72]: Wasm main thread starts 
INFO   |zellij_utils::input::plug| 2023-05-30 18:13:53.355 [async-std/runti] [zellij-utils/src/input/plugins.rs:139]: Plugin 'compact-bar.wasm' exists in the 'PLUGIN DIR' at '/home/m/.local/share/zellij/plugins/' but is being ignored 
WARN   |zellij_utils::ipc        | 2023-05-30 18:14:45.050 [router    ] [zellij-utils/src/ipc.rs:230]: Error in IpcReceiver.recv(): InvalidMarkerRead(Os { code: 104, kind: ConnectionReset, message: "Connection reset by peer" }) 
ERROR  |zellij_client            | 2023-05-30 18:14:45.050 [router    ] [zellij-client/src/lib.rs:309]: Received empty message from server 
```

**Basic information**

`zellij --version`: 0.36.0 
`stty size`: `58 118`
`uname -av` or `ver`(Windows): `Linux hoshi 5.4.243 #1-NixOS SMP Wed May 17 09:36:05 UTC 2023 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

List of programs you interact with as, `PROGRAM --version`: None

**Further information**

This is new with 0.36.0, has not ever happened before.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: zellij 0.33.0 works for me on the same device, so I assume it is a bug with the 0.36.0 version.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Zellij 0.36.0 has been out for a few weeks and this is the first I hear of this issue - so just for context. Not saying it's not a Zellij issue, just that my guess is that this is a bit more involved.

This looks like we're unable to read from an IPC socket. This code has not changed since 0.33.0 (and even before) to the best of my knowledge.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: My first guess would be to check if somehow the new Zellij instance is getting a different runtime directory. Otherwise to sanitize the environment as much as possible, to try and run the precompiled version from the release, to try to run inside a docker containers, etc.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi, thanks for your fast reply!

> Zellij 0.36.0 has been out for a few weeks and this is the first I hear of this issue

I updated yesterday and did not use zellij on this particular device, so that's why I only report it now.

I will try to debug this further tomorrow, if I can find time.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Hm it is indeed interesting! I just noticed that my other device also has 0.36.0 installed and I have no issue there... :<nick>:

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: There's some number of issues related to panicking of wasm plugins like #2078. Something definitely gone wrong with them in 0.36 version. In 0.37.0 everything looks fine.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant2 - these sorts of issues usually have to do with the wrong version of the plugins being loaded. I'm happy to look further into these issues, but just to stress that they almost 100% have to do with the environment: eg. duplicate entries in cache (stemming from having previously compiled git version of the same number), compiling the plugins by hand (my guess about the nix CI in this case) etc.

If this were a sweeping issue there would have been considerably more people reporting it by now (as well as CI failures etc.)

Again, happy to help - but let's look at the environment before we look at changes in the version. I could be wrong but this almost certainly comes from there.

This goes for @reporter as well.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
used to install via `cargo install --git https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij [--force]`. Used everything with default setup without installing any extras or setting up config or layout files. No idea what should affect environment so much it break between versions on defaults.

>considerably more people reporting it 

There's a bunch of opened issues related to [startup crashes](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Azellij-org%2Fzellij+panicked&type=issues), so people were reporting this kind of issues. Definitely this requires some cleanup and I guess you are short on manpower to deal with all of them. Parts of them probably should be closed as dupes. 

> Again, happy to help - but let's look at the environment before we look at changes in the version.

This require specifics what exact environment people should provide to help to help? Something like `echo "$ZELLIJ|$SHELL|$EDITOR|$TERM|$(uname -osr)"`? Specify terminal? Logs?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant2 - you are installing the development branch. I would strongly recommend you install an official release (eg. with `cargo install --locked zellij`). The development branch is prone to exactly these kinds of breakages, because we do not upgrade the plugin version while breaking the API constantly.

EDIT: forgot to mention, also please be sure to remove the cache folder (by default on linux `~/.cache/zellij`) before the first run of the release version in order to clean all the possibly corrupted assets from the development version.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Delete the cache folder resolved the crash for me :+1:

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @reporter - any updates? Can we close this?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
So I did not experience the problem since I opened the issue and with the given information everyone should be able to resolve the issue...

I think we can close this, yes.
